proposed_from.topic: Causal nullity and attainable-rank design in finite proximal treatment multigraphs. For binary outcomes, finite observed proxies, bounded finite latent support, eta-positive observed cells, and strictly positive full-data completions with common W-given-U kernels and shared treatment-node contrast bridges, prove target-population root contrasts are identified exactly when ker(A_P) is contained in ker(R_0). For every violating null direction, construct an explicit nonzero interval of positive full-data perturbations preserving all observed trial and target laws, proxy restrictions, and latent node contrasts while changing the target. In the rank-one trial submodel with common proxy kernel C of rank q, prove generic rank q(|V|-1) exactly when the treatment multigraph contains q edge-disjoint spanning trees; full W-bridge recovery also requires q=|W|. Give matroid-union certificates, separated-rank GLS/Wald inference, and finite-sample Bonferroni Clopper–Pearson cell-region projection covering every compatible contrast without rank selection. Consumer: the NETMOTION neonatal-oxygen IPD network, where added trials cannot overcome the proxy-rank ceiling. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Signed-cell causal lifts were derived and stress-tested on eight heterogeneous two-stratum/four-treatment rational models, preserving 5,120 observed cells and 2,304 latent-CATE equalities. Nonempty attainable-row sets have affine dimension q−1; 258 rectangular-kernel graph cases matched the q-tree rank formula. Rank-two/rank-three parallel-edge designs and exact binomial-tail inversion were checked, including 3,528 multinomial configurations. Boundaries involving q=1, redundant C rows, insufficient trees, zero Z-kernel entries, dependent outcomes, deficient rank, and denominator clearing were tested; no exact literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove the universal signed-cell lifting lemma for arbitrary finite supports, preserving every observed cell and shared latent node contrast simultaneously. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the supplied two-X/four-treatment rational model with dependent outcomes, a zero in a nonconstant Z kernel, and a nonreference left endpoint; apply both perturbation signs at half the explicit radius and verify every equality and positivity condition exactly. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest identification theorem is Proposition 2.3 of \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023}: a linear functional is constant over a conditional-moment solution set exactly when its representer annihilates the operator nullspace. The exact-nullity theorem recovers that algebra after stacking randomized treatment edges, while the signed-cell theorem supplies the missing causal necessity by mapping every algebraic null vector to two full-data laws preserving all observed cells, the common proxy kernel, and shared latent node contrasts. Its primitive support-tangent condition is strictly weaker than positivity of the entire joint potential-outcome cube and gives an explicit positive radius through a support-restricted right inverse. The second headline is not the classical tree-packing or matroid-partition certificate of \cite{NashWilliams1961} and \cite{Edmonds1965}: it is the representation theorem that rows attainable from a rank-\(q_x\) stochastic common kernel make \(A_{P,x}\) attain \(q_x(|V|-1)\) generically exactly at the tree threshold. The resulting minimum-cost augmentation statement is causal because its certificate determines whether added randomized comparisons remove proxy-limited ambiguity. The explicit two-stratum example is not covered by the full-rank condition of \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018}, the two-trial topology of \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026}, or observed-modifier transport in \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023}.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Primary arXiv source, Introduction, Proposition 2.3 and its proof, Theorem 3.4, and Discussion.
seed_details.question: Can every target-relevant element of \(\ker(A_P)\) be lifted to two strictly positive full-data laws preserving all observed cells and latent node contrasts, so that bridge-fiber invariance becomes an exact causal identification criterion?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace variation between two formal bridge solutions in Proposition 2.3 by a signed perturbation of the entire joint potential-outcome cube, with population-specific baseline compensation and an explicit positivity radius.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for proximal causal null spaces, positive causal completions, and multitrial bridge nonuniqueness found no matching universal lift; Su et al. and Xu et al. are the closest trial papers but use two trials and do not prove causal necessity.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Zhang et al. because their Proposition 2.3 already gives the nullspace if-and-only-if.
seed_details.rebuttal: That proposition is an affine bridge-fiber statement; it does not show that an arbitrary null direction is realizable by positive causal laws satisfying all proxy and cross-population restrictions.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Primary arXiv source, Introduction, finite categorical rank condition, Theorem 3.1, and Discussion.
seed_details.question: Does rank \(q\) of a common finite proxy kernel convert treatment-network connectivity into generic operator rank \(q(|V|-1)\), and is \(q\)-tree packing the exact threshold?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Tensor the reduced treatment-incidence representation with the affine row space of the common stochastic proxy kernel and prove noncancellation of the spanning-tree minor polynomial on the attainable row domain.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search located classical tree packing and ordinary graph-optimal treatment design, but no causal or proximal theorem for incidence rows constrained to a stochastic kernel image.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Nash-Williams after replacing each edge by \(q\) colored copies.
seed_details.rebuttal: The observed rows are not freely colored copies; the changed step is proving that the positive attainable image of one common kernel realizes the required generic matrix representation and that its minors do not cancel.

seed_details.question: When \(R_0\ker(A_P)\ne\{0\}\), is the sharp network contrast set the projection of a finite positive full-data completion region, including a support-sensitive characterization of attained and open endpoints?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace proxy-ratio envelopes for one treatment with joint optimization over a shared-kernel, shared-node-contrast completion across all trial edges, using the causal lift to prove sharpness rather than optimizing over bridges alone.
seed_details.destination_search: No located proximal bounds paper imposes a treatment multigraph and simultaneous latent node contrasts; the closest projection theory is Kaido et al., which addresses inference rather than causal sharpness.
seed_details.red_team: A finite model makes the identified set a routine polynomial program.
seed_details.rebuttal: Writing a program is not sharpness: the unresolved content is equivalence between projected algebraic solutions and actual positive latent completions with shared restrictions and support-sensitive endpoint attainment.

seed_details.destination_search: Searches for proximal support-face tangent cones and sparse proxy causal completions found no exact criterion; current bounds work gives valid envelopes, not a completion-fiber cone.
seed_details.red_team: Farkas' lemma makes boundary identification automatic once the zero pattern is fixed.
seed_details.rebuttal: The cone includes coupled normalization, observed-cell, proxy, and latent-CATE constraints; deriving its primitive observable representation is the open mathematical content.
seed_details.drop_reason: Kept as the first-class open-ended question because feasibility is too uncertain for the cold-start headline theorem.

seed_details.question: Can a truncated-pseudoinverse estimator have a representative-invariant influence function and uniform Gaussian law on each separated identified rank stratum of a finite proximal network?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the fixed-rank pseudoinverse and show that the terms depending on the nonunique bridge vanish after left multiplication by \(R_0\) because \(R_0\ker(A_P)=0\).
seed_details.destination_search: Strong-functional inference is occupied in general conditional-moment models, but the finite network's rank-stratified derivative and exact transition to set identification are not covered.
seed_details.red_team: This is an immediate delta-method corollary of Bennett et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: The core cancellation is specialized but nontrivial at deficient fixed rank; nevertheless, the general inference theory is close enough that this belongs as a supporting theorem, not the headline.
seed_details.drop_reason: Downgraded to a secondary theorem because the general strong-functional limit theory is already well developed.

seed_details.question: Can simultaneous exact multinomial cell regions be projected through the finite bridge equations to cover the entire causal identified set at every rank without preliminary rank selection?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace asymptotic calibrated moment relaxation by marginal exact binomial inversion and prove that one simultaneous primitive event deterministically contains every compatible causal contrast after projection.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found asymptotic projection methods and exact univariate binomial intervals, but no finite-sample causal network projection through a rank-changing proximal completion model.
seed_details.red_team: Bonferroni followed by deterministic projection is a textbook coverage argument.
seed_details.rebuttal: The guarantee is valid and useful, but the objection caps its ambition; it is retained only as an honesty layer around the deeper identification theorem.
seed_details.drop_reason: Supporting inference result rather than a standalone proposal kernel.

seed_details.question: Can conditioning on proximal singular-value strength yield one Wald procedure valid as a network contrast crosses from strong point identification to partial identification?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the weak-IV reduced-form Gaussian experiment by the constrained multinomial limit experiment for \((A_P,b_P,R_0)\), retaining positivity and target-functional nullspace geometry.
seed_details.destination_search: Conditional Wald is available for weak IV and nonlinear GMM, but no source integrates a rank-changing causal identified set with positive-completion constraints.
seed_details.red_team: The proximal cell moments are finite-dimensional GMM, so Lee et al.'s critical values apply directly.
seed_details.rebuttal: At exact rank deficiency the causal target becomes a set projection, not merely a weakly identified point parameter; importing the GMM statistic does not establish coverage of all positive completions.
seed_details.drop_reason: The limit experiment and conditioning statistic require a separate paper; exact projection supplies a feasible fallback in this proposal.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel sits at the intersection of four lines. First, \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018} and \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023} establish finite-proxy rank identification and invariance of selected functionals under bridge nonuniqueness. Second, \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026} identifies a proximal transported contrast for one source and one target trial, while \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023} handles multiple trials using observed modifiers; \cite{XuEtAl2026} remains a two-trial parametric reconciliation framework. Third, \cite{NashWilliams1961} supplies the exact tree-packing partition criterion and \cite{Rosa2018} relates ordinary treatment-contrast information to graph Laplacians; the constrained incidence--proxy rank problem is absent from both. Fourth, \cite{BennettEtAl2023}, \cite{KaidoMolinariStoye2019}, and \cite{LeeEtAl2023} provide, respectively, inference for strongly identified functionals, asymptotic calibrated projection, and weak-identification conditional Wald methods. None of the opened primary sources contains the universal positive causal lift, the attainable rank-\(q\) tree theorem, or an exact finite-cell projection for a proximal trial multigraph.
